name: Pratte's Reef (permit name: Chevron Reef)

confidence.reason: The outline is traced on the reef designer's own scaled plan drawing (Skelly Engineering design layout, 110 bags + 30 optional, also published as the 'design layout' in Borrero & Nelsen 2003), using only the solid-outline bags; the printed scale bar agrees with the known bag size (4 x 7 x 10 ft = 7.9 m3) within about 3-6% and two reproductions of the drawing agree to about 1% in area. It is a design drawing, not a survey or photo: nothing of the structure is visible on any image (removed 2008-2010), the April 2001 second phase (90 more bags, crest widened) is not drawn, the built bags moved and sank, and the map position cannot be fixed.
factors: + Scaled drawing from the designer of record (Skelly Engineering) with a printed scale bar (0-15-30-60-90 ft); the bar ticks fit a straight line to within 0.5 px in both reproductions (img1, img5) and the two reproductions are related by a near-uniform affine map (x scale 0.8763 vs 0.8783 expected from the bars, 0.2% apart; y scale 1.5% lower)

+ Independent scale check (verification 2026-10-05): ICCE-2010 gives the Pratte's bag as 7.9 m3 maximum volume; a secondary web summary (primary not located) gives the bag as 4 x 7 x 10 ft = 280 ft3 = 7.93 m3, which matches ICCE's figure by arithmetic. The drawing's bag grid, measured on both reproductions, has a column pitch of 6.8-6.9 ft (bag width 7 ft) and a row pitch of 9.4-9.6 ft (bag length 10 ft), i.e. 1-6% below nominal; spine block 10.6 m for 5 columns (2.12 m each) and 14.1 m for 5 rows (2.82 m each)

+ Solid-outline bags only: the drawing legend shows 110 solid + 30 dashed 'optional' bags; the 30 dashed bags are the outer two rows on each arm near the apex and the left column of the spine, and are excluded (this verification removed about 49 m2 of dashed-bag area that the first trace had wrongly included)

+ Arm angles 44.7 / 44.4 deg to the V axis (printed 45; re-measured on the canonical polygon: long edges at 43.7-46.5 deg), spine block 5 x 5 bag grid. NOTE the printed crest label '-6 ft MSL' (1.83 m below MSL = about 0.97 m below MLLW, using NOAA Los Angeles datums MSL = MLLW + 2.82 ft) does NOT match ICCE-2010's '1.8 m below MLLW at the outermost point after installation' (different datum and quantity); it is close to the post-Phase-II crest (-0.9 m MLLW, RWR). The crest depth therefore cannot identify which phase the drawing shows; the bag count (110) does

- Design drawing only (Phase I, 110 bags). Phase II (April 2001, +90 bags, volume +80%, crest widened and made shallower, bags placed directly over the Phase I bags - ICCE 2010 p.7) is NOT drawn: the final reef was higher and wider at the crest than this footprint, by an unknown amount, and it is unknown whether any of the 30 optional bags were built

- Bags were crane-placed, moved, sank and were buried (Borrero 2010; RWR), so the real footprint differed from the design by metres; no as-built survey, multibeam plot or aerial photo could be retrieved (Borrero & Nelsen 2003 figures and the CCRP aerials are blocked: HTTP 403)
- Drawing has no north arrow; orientation (+x toward SSE) is inferred from the 1996 concept plan (north arrow) and the present shoreline (155.5 deg, own fit)

- Published coordinates disagree by 100s of metres (card/Wikipedia is 288 m offshore of today's dry-sand edge; RWR and Gemini coordinates are 113-119 m), and all three lie SOUTH of the short rock groin at 33.91685,-118.43030 (taken to be the Grand Street jetty) whereas the CCC staff report (300 yd north of the Grand Avenue jetty) and Borrero & Nelsen 2003 (about 200 m south of the Hyperion 1-mile outfall, within 500 m of it and of the Grand Street jetty) put the reef NORTH of that jetty; so no lat/lon polygon is given (geo = null)

- Outline position depends on the stroke edge: +-1 px = +-0.2 m = about +-4% area; solid/dashed classification of the edge rows adds about +-10 m2; scale-bar anisotropy between reproductions about 1.5%

+ (2026-10-05, not yet re-verified) the primary 2003 paper confirms the bag size (4 x 7 x 10 ft, 7.9 m3), the Phase I count (110) and the 30 m cross-shore extent (p.14) against the 28.6 m of the outline (-4.7 %); it reprints the same drawing as Fig. 4. It does NOT contain an as-built plan, so confidence stays medium; the datum of the crest label is ambiguous (drawing '-6' MSL' vs paper '-6 ft MLLW': same number, 0.85 m apart)

design_version.drawn: Phase I design, fall 2000: 110 solid-outline geotextile bags (about 3.0 m x 2.2 m x 1.2 m each) in a V of two arms at 45 deg to the wave direction, with a 5 x 5 bag spine block at the apex. The 30 dashed 'optional' bags on the drawing are not part of the outline. This is NOT the final reef: Phase II (April 2001) put 90 more bags on top of these and widened the crest.
design_version.why_this_one: It is the only plan view of the built design found (Skelly Engineering title block, printed BAG COUNT 110 = the documented Phase I count) and it is later than the 1996 concept (about 30 large bags). No plan, survey or aerial photo of the post-Phase-II reef was retrievable, so the Phase I design footprint is the best available drawing; the page must say that the final (200-bag) reef was higher and wider at the crest than the footprint shown. Verification 2026-10-05: the same drawing (BAG COUNT 110, OPTIONAL BAGS 30, TOP OF BAG MIN DEPTH -6' MSL, 0-15-30-60-90 ft bar, Skelly Engineering title block) is Fig. 4 'The design layout of Pratte's Reef' of Borrero & Nelsen (2003) (viewed on ResearchGate; the full text beyond page 1 is paywalled) and Fig. 2.10 of Henriquez (2005), and RWR says 'The initial plan called for 110 bags'. Everything published labels it the DESIGN layout; no as-built plan was found, and RWR/Borrero report that the placed bags moved, sank and were buried (first winter swells covered the reef in 2000-01), so the real Phase I footprint differed from the drawing by an unknown amount. WHAT THE DRAWING REPRESENTS (state this on the page): the Phase I design layout, fall 2000, solid-outline bags only, not the as-built and not the 200-bag reef of April 2001. UPDATE 2026-10-05: Borrero & Nelsen (2003), now in hand as a file (src/borrero_nelsen_2003_prattes_monitoring_results.pdf), reprints this drawing as its Fig. 4 'The design layout of Pratte's Reef' and has no as-built plan, so the DESIGN-layout conclusion stands; design_version.drawn is unchanged.

alternatives_seen.what: 1996 conceptual plan: about 30 large geobags, V of two 150 ft wings, about 9,000 sq ft, 5,000 yd3; permit application E-98-15, CCC hearing Oct 1998
alternatives_seen.why_not_used: Earlier concept, superseded when the budget fell and the design changed to 110 small (7.9 m3) bags; the sketch is also not to scale (the two '150 ft' dimension lines measure 237 and 279 px). Used only for orientation and as an arm-length cross-check.

alternatives_seen.what: Phase II state (about 200 bags in total, 23-24 April 2001): 90 new bags, +80% volume, crest widened and made shallower (to within 1 m of MLLW), new bags placed directly over the Phase I bags
alternatives_seen.why_not_used: Text only (ICCE 2010 p.7; Wikipedia 'Chevron Reef' gives the bag count; RWR says 'on top of the existing bags'). No plan or survey of it was retrievable (Borrero & Nelsen 2003 figures and Coastal Frontiers' 2008 reef-outline mapping exist but are not public). The Phase I plan footprint is therefore the base of the final structure, but the crest was wider and the plan extent after Phase II is unknown.

alternatives_seen.what: 30 optional bags drawn dashed on the Skelly drawing (outer two rows of each arm near the apex + left column of the spine: about 12-13 per arm + 5)

Gemini: 40 m x 20 m, 650 m2 (496 m2 in another file; its own reef_footprints.json also carries 57.8 x 31.2 m / 584 m2 'per Skelly 2001 permit drawing')

Fig. 2 is a small (432 x 231 px) annotated aerial photo with a 'Reef' text label only, no reef outline and no scale; not retrievable as a file (ResearchGate image hosts return HTTP 403 to scripts), viewed in the browser pane only. scale.evidence: Printed bar 'SCALE: 1in=30ft' with ticks labelled 15', 30', 60', 90' (the 0 tick is cut off by the image edge). Run-length scan of bar rows 329-331 gives tick positions x = 21, 44, 92, 138.5 px (re-measured in verification). Least-squares fit px = -3.22 + 1.5712*ft (residuals <= 0.45 px) -> 1.5712 px/ft = 5.1549 px/m (0.1940 m/px). Cross-checks: (1) img5 (the same drawing, 1.139x larger) has its own bar fit 1.7889 px/ft; an 87-cell centroid-matched affine fit img5->img1 gives x scale 0.8763 (bars predict 0.8783, 0.2% apart) and y scale 0.8651 (1.5% lower: the two reproductions differ slightly in aspect). (2) Bag size: ICCE-2010 Fig. 1 gives 'A Pratte's Reef bag' 3 m long x 1.2 m high, volume 7.9 m3, implied plan width 7.9/(3 x 1.2) = 2.2 m; the drawing's spine block is 10.6 m wide for 5 columns (2.12 m each) and 14.1 m tall for 5 rows (2.82 m each, i.e. 6-7% below the 3.0 m bag length; verification re-measurement, the first trace said 13.8 m).

sources.traced_what: Outer boundary (outline centre-line) of the SOLID-outlined bags only = the 110 Phase I bags: the 5 x 5 spine block plus both 45-degree bag arms. The 30 dashed-outline 'optional bags' (outer two rows beside each elbow and the spine's left column) are excluded on both arms and on the spine.
sources.match_notes: Verification 2026-10-05: the first trace (66 vertices, 483.9 m2) wrongly included about 49 m2 of dashed-bag area (lower arm: both outer dashed rows, continuity along the outline edge 0.61-0.68; upper arm: second dashed row, 0.65-0.82; a solid line scores 0.95-1.00). The outline was re-derived by shifting those edges inward to the first continuous (solid) stroke, found on img5 where the dash gaps are resolved (edge-continuity profiles across both arms), mapped to img1 with the 87-cell affine and intersected with the original img1 trace (+0.5 px tolerance), so the img1 outline is the original trace wherever it already sat on solid lines. 76 vertices, 435.2 m2. Edge directions of the new outline: upper arm +45.1, +45.0, +43.7, +44.8 deg, lower arm -43.5, -44.4, -44.5, -45.3 deg from the horizontal (all long edges parallel to the arms, as expected for edges on real bag rows). Overlay: overlays/img1_final.png (new), overlays/img1_correction_red_new_cyan_old.png, old overlays in overlays/_pre_verification/. Sensitivity: +-1 px = +-4% area.

canonical.frame: metres; origin = assumed shoreline point on the V axis, 91.44 m (100 yd, text value) inshore of the polygon centroid; +x alongshore toward ~155 deg (SSE, the side of the drawing's lower arm); +y offshore toward ~245 deg (WSW) (+y = +x turned 90 deg clockwise, the tools/geom.py convention). The drawing has no north arrow: the orientation assumes its horizontal 'wave direction' axis is the shore-normal (supported to ~5 deg by the 1996 concept plan and the present shoreline, see angles)
canonical.distance_offshore_basis: TEXT value (CCC staff report E-98-15 p.1: '100 yards offshore ... in about 15 feet of water' for the 1996 concept; Wikipedia 'Chevron Reef' about 100 yards; RWR 'roughly 100 meters off the beach'). Not measurable from the drawing; it only fixes where the canonical polygon sits along y (polygon y-range 74.7 to 103.3 m). It is the distance of the reef centre, from an undefined shoreline.
canonical.shore_normal_note: offshore direction = present shoreline bearing 155.5/335.5 deg (own robust fit to the dry-sand edge on the 2026-01-09 Esri image, 92 inlier rows, +-2) turned to the sea side = 245.5 deg; the 1996 concept plan (img6) puts the V bisector at 61 deg (onshore), i.e. 241 deg offshore
canonical.transform_note: Pixel -> metres by the explicit formula x = (py - oy)/px_per_m, y = -(px - ox)/px_per_m with origin (ox,oy) = (628.5, 156.2) px on img1 (placed so the polygon centroid is at x=0, y=91.44 m) and px_per_m = 5.1549. Verified in the 2026-10-05 verification against the FIXED tools/geom.py make-canonical (--alongshore-dir-px 0,1): all 76 vertices agree to 0.0000 m; one vertex checked by hand: px (96.16, 123.82) -> x = (123.82-156.2)/5.1549 = -6.281 m, y = -(96.16-628.5)/5.1549 = 103.269 m. (The pre-fix tool rotated by +phi and would have been wrong for this direction.) Re-checked in the third verification run (2026-10-05): the fixed tools/geom.py make-canonical (--origin-px 628.5,156.2 --alongshore-dir-px 0,1, --no-write on a copy) reproduces all 76 vertices of polygons_m to 0.007 m (the 2-decimal rounding), area 435.21 m2, bbox 58.02 x 28.63 m, max dimension 58.03 m; geom.py selftest = 334 checks, 0 failed; vertex 0 re-derived by hand (px 96.16,123.82 -> x = -6.281, y = 103.269 m). Handedness check: with page-up = 335 deg the drawing's upper arm points to bearing 20 deg and the lower arm to 110 deg, matching the 1996 concept plan (16 and 106 deg), so the frame is not mirrored.

gemini.summary: Gemini's 40 x 20 m (650 m2) cannot be traced to any retrievable source and is contradicted by the scaled drawing. The only dimensioned plan found (Skelly Engineering, scaled, 110 solid + 30 optional bags; also Fig. 4 of Borrero & Nelsen 2003 and Fig. 2.10 of Henriquez 2005) gives a solid-bag envelope of about 58 x 29 m and 435 m2 (about 515 m2 if the optional bags are counted), i.e. Gemini's length is ~31% too short, its width ~30% too narrow, and its 650 m2 is inconsistent with its own 40 x 20 m. Gemini's other file (reef_footprints.json: 57.8 x 31.2 m, 584 m2) is a coarse polygon of the same drawing that includes the optional bags: right tip-to-tip, 34% too much area. Gemini's 1.8 m crest depth is ICCE-2010's as-installed Phase I value (below MLLW); it should not be compared with the drawing's '-6 ft MSL' (about 0.97 m below MLLW). The CCC permit number it cites (5-97-283) is not in the real record (E-98-15). Its Henriquez, CCC, Coastal Frontiers, decommissioning and image26 verdicts were re-checked and stand.

geo_note: No lat/lon polygon: three published coordinates disagree by up to 313 m alongshore (card/Wikipedia 33.915,-118.4325; Gemini 33.9162,-118.4312; RWR page 33.913666,-118.429733) and none can be tied to the structure (removed 2008-2010; no pre-removal georeferenced image retrievable). All three lie south of the short rock groin at 33.91685,-118.43030 (assumed to be the Grand Street/Grand Avenue jetty: the only groin in the 800 m crop), whereas two primary sources put the reef north of the Grand Street jetty: CCC staff report E-98-15 (300 yd north of it, 100 yd offshore, 1996-98 siting) and Borrero & Nelsen 2003 (about 200 m south of the Hyperion 1-mile outfall, within 500 m of the outfall and the jetty, aerial figure labels 'Reef' between them). A text-only estimate from the CCC figures (274 m along the 335.5 deg shoreline from the groin, 91 m offshore toward 245.5 deg) is about 33.9188,-118.4324 with an uncertainty of +-150 m or worse; it is NOT used for any polygon and is listed only as a hint for a page marker labelled 'position approximate'. The RWR page coordinate (about 350 m south of that groin) contradicts both primary sources. UPDATE 2026-10-05 (3D run, Borrero & Nelsen 2003 supplied by Lior): Fig. 9 of that paper is a vector bathymetry window on a UTM zone 11N grid (E 367,449-367,561 m, N 3,754,239-3,754,311 m; contours -1..-4 m, Oct 2000 and Mar 2001); its centre is 33.92058 N, -118.43335 E. The paper says the reef is 'approximately 200 m south of the Hyperion 1-mile outfall'; the outfall landfall read on the Navionics chart (33.9231 N, -118.4337, +-20 m) + 200-318 m south along 155 deg + 91 m offshore gives 33.9202-33.9211 N, -118.4332..-118.4337, within 35 m of the window centre. INFERRED position hint 33.92058, -118.43335 (+-100 m); it lies 217 m NNW of the earlier text-derived hint (33.9188, -118.4324) and supersedes it. geo stays null: the reef outline is not drawn in Fig. 9, so there is no georeferenced polygon.
